presentation.title: Package Delivery Text Scam
presentation.summary: Practice responding to an unexpected package text, a fake tracking website, an address-confirmation request, and a small redelivery-fee scam.
presentation.practiceGoal: Pause when a delivery message supplies urgency and its own link, then verify the package through a merchant or carrier source you locate independently.

warningSigns.sign: The message arrives from an unfamiliar number and does not name the recipient, merchant, or package.
The sender creates a short deadline and supplies the only link for solving the problem.
The website uses professional-looking branding but an unfamiliar domain and no legitimate tracking history.
The page collects personal information before revealing a small redelivery fee.
A countdown pressures the learner to submit complete card and billing details.

finalReview.safestAction: Delete or close the supplied message and link, then check the order through the merchant or carrier app, website, or phone number you locate independently.

realWorldActions.action: Do not rely on a logo, sender name, or link supplied by an unexpected text.
Block and report the message as junk or spam.
If personal information was entered, watch for convincing follow-up delivery, banking, or account scams.
If ordinary card information was submitted, contact the issuer immediately, lock or replace the card, and review transactions.
Change a password only if a real account password was entered.

artifact.heading: Address confirmation required
artifact.message: ParcelRoute Delivery: We could not deliver your package because the address information is incomplete. Confirm your address within 12 hours or the package will be returned to sender: parcelroute-reschedule.com/8K2M
artifact.transcript: An older adult is expecting at least one package this week but does not know the carrier. A text from an unfamiliar number claims that ParcelRoute Delivery could not deliver a package because the address is incomplete. It demands confirmation within 12 hours and supplies parcelroute-reschedule.com/8K2M. The message does not identify the recipient, merchant, package contents, or real tracking history. ParcelRoute Delivery is fictional.

scene.question: What would you do with this unexpected delivery text?
scene.description: You are expecting a package sometime this week, but you do not know which carrier will deliver it.

warningSigns.sign: The sender is unfamiliar.
No merchant, recipient, package, or earlier tracking history is identified.
The text creates a 12-hour deadline and supplies its own link.

choice.title: Tap the link to identify the package
choice.subtitle: Open the website supplied by the unfamiliar sender.

feedback.heading: The sender chose the website for you
feedback.consequence: The link opens a page controlled by whoever sent the text.
feedback.explanation: Expecting a package makes the story believable, but it does not verify this sender or link. A safer check begins in an app or website you locate yourself.

warningSigns.sign: The text provides both the problem and the only route to fix it.
The message gives no specific package details.

choice.title: Delete the text and check officially
choice.subtitle: Open the merchant or carrier app or website independently.

feedback.heading: You chose a source the sender does not control
feedback.consequence: The suspicious link stays closed and no information is shared.
feedback.explanation: Official tracking found through a saved app, typed address, or independently located phone number can confirm the real delivery status.

warningSigns.sign: The original text omitted information that real order tracking can provide.
The deadline tried to rush you away from independent checking.

choice.title: Reply “STOP”
choice.subtitle: Ask the unfamiliar sender to stop texting.

feedback.heading: A reply does not verify or resolve the claim
feedback.consequence: The sender knows the number is active and can send another urgent message.
feedback.explanation: “STOP” can be useful with legitimate subscribed messages, but it does not prove this sender is a carrier or fix a supposed delivery problem.

warningSigns.sign: The sender has not shown that this is a legitimate subscription.
The same unknown number still controls the conversation.

artifact.heading: Unsubscribe request received
artifact.message: Unsubscribe request received. Your delivery still requires action. Package will be returned today unless the address is confirmed: parcelroute-reschedule.com/8K2M
artifact.transcript: After the learner replies STOP, another message says the unsubscribe request was received but the delivery still requires action. It claims the package will be returned today unless the address is confirmed through the same link. The reply did not verify the sender or resolve any real delivery issue.

scene.question: How would you respond to this increased pressure?
scene.description: The supposed deadline has changed from 12 hours to “today,” but no package details have appeared.

warningSigns.sign: The sender continues after the STOP reply.
The deadline becomes more urgent without evidence.
The same link is repeated.

choice.title: Tap the link before the package is returned
choice.subtitle: Act on the new deadline.

feedback.heading: Escalating urgency is meant to overcome caution
feedback.consequence: The sender's repeated link opens the same unverified website.
feedback.explanation: A changed deadline is not proof. The sender still has not identified a real shipment.

warningSigns.sign: The urgency increased after you tried to stop.
No official tracking history was provided.

choice.title: Block and report, then check official tracking
choice.subtitle: End contact and use a source you locate independently.

feedback.heading: You ended the sender's pressure
feedback.consequence: The sender is blocked, the text is reported, and no personal information is entered.
feedback.explanation: Independent tracking can answer the delivery question without relying on the suspicious sender.

warningSigns.sign: The sender ignored the meaning of your STOP reply.
The sender continued to demand use of its own link.

choice.title: Reply and ask which package it is
choice.subtitle: Keep communicating with the sender for more details.

feedback.heading: The sender controls any answer it gives
feedback.consequence: The conversation continues and the sender receives another sign that the number is active.
feedback.explanation: Details supplied by the same unverified sender cannot independently prove a shipment exists.

warningSigns.sign: The original text omitted the merchant and package.

artifact.heading: Shipment details unavailable
artifact.message: Shipment details are unavailable until the delivery address is confirmed. Use the secure link to continue.
artifact.transcript: The learner asks which package is being delivered. The sender refuses to identify it and says shipment details are unavailable until the delivery address is confirmed through the supplied “secure” link. Calling a link secure does not make it legitimate.

scene.question: What would you do after the sender avoids the question?
scene.description: You now have a clear opportunity to stop and verify the package independently.

warningSigns.sign: The sender withholds basic shipment details.
The sender labels its own link “secure” without proof.

choice.title: Stop replying and verify officially
choice.subtitle: Use the merchant account, carrier app, or an independently located phone number.

feedback.heading: The refusal is a reason to change channels
feedback.consequence: The conversation ends before the sender receives personal information.
feedback.explanation: Real order history can identify the merchant, status, and tracking events without requiring an unfamiliar text link.

warningSigns.sign: The sender could not name the shipment.

choice.title: Open the supplied link
choice.subtitle: Try the website after the sender refuses to provide details.

feedback.heading: The unanswered question remains important
feedback.consequence: The unverified sender directs you to a website it controls.
feedback.explanation: A secure-looking page cannot replace independently verified tracking information.

artifact.heading: Delivery Attempt Unsuccessful
artifact.message: We could not confirm your address. Update your information now to prevent the package from being returned. Tracking reference: PR-8K2M-DELIVERY. ParcelRoute Delivery is fictional, and this page provides no merchant, recipient, or legitimate tracking history.
artifact.transcript: A professional-looking fictional ParcelRoute page appears at parcelroute-reschedule.com. It shows a package icon, vague tracking reference PR-8K2M-DELIVERY, and the heading “Delivery Attempt Unsuccessful.” It says the address could not be confirmed and must be updated now. It does not identify a real merchant, recipient, package, or tracking history.

scene.question: What matters most when judging this professional-looking page?
scene.description: Logos, package icons, and polished layouts can be copied. The actual domain and independently verified tracking history matter more.

warningSigns.sign: The domain is parcelroute-reschedule.com, not a site independently located by the learner.
The tracking reference is vague and has no prior events.

warningSigns.sign: The page came from an unexpected text.

warningSigns.sign: The domain was supplied by the suspicious text.

warningSigns.sign: The message and website support each other's claims but come from the same source.

artifact.heading: Confirm that you are the intended recipient
artifact.message: This information is required to verify that you are the intended recipient.
artifact.transcript: The fake ParcelRoute page at parcelroute-reschedule.com displays an address-confirmation form. It requests full name, street address, phone number, and email address, claiming the information is required to verify the intended recipient. No payment request has appeared yet.

scene.question: How much information would you give this unverified page?
scene.description: The form appears before any redelivery-fee request. Even partial information can be useful to a scammer.

warningSigns.sign: The package is still unidentified.
The page requested more information than needed to view ordinary tracking.

choice.title: Enter only the street address

feedback.heading: Partial information still has value
feedback.consequence: The scammer receives a real address that can be paired with the active phone number.
feedback.explanation: An address can help later scams feel specific and believable, even when no other fields are completed.

warningSigns.sign: The sender already knows the phone number is active.
The address is being entered on an unverified site.

feedback.heading: You stopped before sharing information

artifact.heading: Address confirmed
artifact.message: A redelivery fee is required before the package can be released. Redelivery fee: $1.95. Complete payment within 10 minutes to prevent return to sender.
artifact.transcript: Only after the learner submitted full personal information does the fake page say “Address confirmed” and reveal a $1.95 redelivery fee. A 10-minute countdown appears. The payment form requests name on card, full card number, expiration date, security code, and billing ZIP code. The small amount is meant to feel harmless; the scammer's real goal is card and identity information.

scene.question: What would you do when the small fee finally appears?
scene.description: The site already received name, address, phone number, and email address. The $1.95 amount and countdown are tactics.

warningSigns.sign: The payment request appeared only after personal information was collected.

warningSigns.sign: The $1.95 fee was revealed after data collection.
